source.title: SilverSummit Healthplan, Inc. SFY 2025 Compliance Review
source.publisher: Nevada Division of Health Care Financing and Policy / Health Services Advisory Group

cards.requirement: The member may file an appeal orally or in writing. With the written consent of the member, a provider or an authorized representative may request an appeal on behalf of the member. If an appeal is filed orally, the MCO documents the contact for tracking purposes and to establish the earliest date of receipt. The MCO must not require the member to submit a written appeal after making an oral appeal.

If the MCO denies a request for expedited resolution of an appeal, it transfers the appeal to the time frame for standard resolution, makes reasonable efforts to give the member prompt oral notice of the delay, and within two calendar days gives the member written notice of the reason for denying the expedited appeal resolution time frame and informs the member of the right to file a grievance if the member disagrees.
cards.required_action: If the MCO denies a request for expedited resolution of an appeal, it must make reasonable efforts to give the member prompt oral notice of the delay and within two calendar days give the member written notice of the reason for the decision to deny the expedited appeal resolution time frame and inform the member of the right to file a grievance if the member disagrees. The MCO must ensure that letters are populated correctly and do not contain any errors.

cards.requirement: The MCO acknowledges receipt of each appeal.
cards.required_action: The MCO must acknowledge receipt of each appeal. The MCO must also ensure that acknowledgement is provided to the member for appeals submitted by a provider on behalf of the member as the member is a party to the appeal.

cards.requirement: The MCO ensures that individuals who make decisions on appeals were not involved in a previous level of review or decision-making, have appropriate clinical expertise when required, and take into account all comments, documents, records, and other information submitted by the member or representative.
The MCO treats oral inquiries seeking to appeal an adverse benefit determination as appeals.

The MCO provides the member a reasonable opportunity, in person and in writing, to present evidence and testimony and make legal and factual arguments. The MCO informs the member of the limited time available for this sufficiently in advance of the resolution time frame for appeals in the case of expedited resolution.
cards.required_action: The MCO must provide the member with a reasonable opportunity, in person and in writing, to present evidence and testimony and make legal and factual arguments. The MCO must inform the member of the limited time available for this sufficiently in advance of the resolution time frame for appeals in the case of expedited resolution.

cards.requirement: The MCO provides the member and his or her representative the member's case file, including medical records, other documents and records, and any new or additional evidence considered, relied upon, or generated by the MCO in connection with the appeal of the adverse benefit determination. This information is provided free of charge and sufficiently in advance of the appeal resolution time frame.
cards.required_action: The MCO must provide the member and his or her representative with the member's case file, including medical records, other documents and records, and any new or additional evidence considered, relied upon, or generated by the MCO in connection with the appeal of the adverse benefit determination. This information must be provided free of charge and sufficiently in advance of the resolution time frame for appeals.

cards.requirement: The MCO resolves standard appeals and sends written notice to the affected parties as expeditiously as the member's health condition requires, but no later than 30 calendar days from the day the MCO receives the appeal.
cards.required_action: The MCO must resolve standard appeals and send written notice to the affected parties as expeditiously as the member's health condition requires, but no later than 30 calendar days from the day the MCO receives the appeal.

cards.requirement: The MCO resolves expedited appeals and sends written notice to the affected parties no later than 72 hours after the MCO receives the appeal.

If the MCO extends the standard or expedited appeal resolution time frames not at the request of the member, it makes reasonable efforts to give the member prompt oral notice of the delay, gives written notice within two calendar days explaining the extension and grievance right, and resolves the appeal no later than the date the extension expires.
If the MCO fails to adhere to the appeal notice and timing requirements, the member is deemed to have exhausted the MCO's appeals process and may initiate a State fair hearing.
cards.required_action: If the MCO fails to adhere to the appeal notice and timing requirements, the member is deemed to have exhausted the MCO's appeals process. The MCO must mail the member a written notice when the time frame expires, informing the member that the MCO failed to complete the appeal in a timely manner and that the member may initiate a State fair hearing.

cards.requirement: For all appeals, the MCO provides written notice of the appeal resolution that includes the results and completion date and, when the appeal is not resolved wholly in favor of the member, the right to request a State fair hearing, the right to request and receive benefits while the hearing is pending, and possible liability for those benefits if the hearing decision upholds the MCO's adverse benefit determination.
For notice of a standard and expedited appeal resolution, the MCO makes a good faith effort to provide oral notice of the disposition in addition to the required written notice.
cards.required_action: For notice of a standard and expedited appeal resolution, the MCO must make a good faith effort to provide oral notice of the disposition in addition to the required written notice.

cards.requirement: The member may request a State fair hearing only after receiving notice that the MCO is upholding the adverse benefit determination related to the appeal. With the written consent of the member, a provider or an authorized representative may request a State fair hearing on behalf of the member.
The member has 90 calendar days from the date of the MCO's notice of appeal resolution to request a State fair hearing.
cards.required_action: The MCO must ensure that the member has 90 calendar days from the date of the MCO's notice of appeal resolution to request a State fair hearing.

cards.requirement: The MCO continues the member's benefits when the member timely appeals, the appeal involves termination, suspension, or reduction of previously authorized services, the services were ordered by an authorized provider, the original authorization has not expired, and the member timely requests continuation of benefits.
